model_annotation: The line plot visualizes the Accuracy (ACC) percentage as a function of Co-occurrence Number across different models. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," exhibits a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^1 to 10^3, with tick labels at each significant power of ten. The y-axis, representing Accuracy percentage with labels in increments of 5%, spans from 40% to just above 65%. The plot contains six lines, each denoting a model, distinguished by unique markers and colors: Base (solid line, circle), FT (dashed line, triangle), MEND (dotted line, diamond), MEMI (solid line with squares, inverted triangle), IKE (dash-dot line, star), and ROME (solid line with plus signs, cross). Starting at the lowest co-occurrence number, the accuracy of Base, FT, and MEMI begins at below 50% and shows a steady increase as the Co-occurrence Number rises. MEND and IKE exhibit similar patterns, starting just above 50%, with EMCI showing a small degree of plateau. ROME line displays a more gradual ascent throughout, starting from above 50% and surpassing all others to reach nearly 65% by the highest co-occurrence number. Each model's final accuracy points for the highest co-occurrence appear to be: Base (exact point not provided), FT (exact point not provided), MEND (exact point not provided), MEMI (exact point not provided), IKE (exact point not provided), and ROME (just above 65%).
